stem: TuxPixel’s new build server runs Rocky Linux, an Enterprise Linux-based distribution. Which tools manage software packages on it? (Choose TWO.)

options.rationale: dnf installs, updates and removes packages from repositories on Enterprise Linux and Fedora, and resolves dependencies.
rpm is the low-level tool for the RPM package format that Enterprise Linux uses; it works on single package files.
apt belongs to the Debian family (Debian, Ubuntu, Raspberry Pi OS).
zypper is the package manager of the SUSE family.
apk is Alpine Linux’s package manager.

explanation: Each distribution family has its own package tools: dpkg and apt for Debian, rpm and dnf for Enterprise Linux, rpm and zypper for SUSE, and apk for Alpine.

stem: Mira needs a free office suite with a word processor, a spreadsheet and a slide editor for the studio’s budget and pitch decks. Which program fits?

options.rationale: GIMP edits raster images such as photos and pixel art.
Thunderbird is an email client.
LibreOffice bundles Writer, Calc and Impress.
VLC plays audio and video files.

explanation: LibreOffice is the open source office suite: a word processor (Writer), a spreadsheet (Calc) and presentations (Impress).

stem: Ada wants a desktop program for her email, calendar and news feeds that is not a web browser. Which one is it?

options.rationale: Thunderbird is Mozilla’s email, calendar and news client.
Visual Studio Code is a code editor, not a mail program.
Inkscape draws vector graphics.
VLC plays media files.

explanation: Thunderbird is the open source mail client from the makers of Firefox, while Firefox is the browser.

stem: What is the relationship between Chromium and Google Chrome?

options.text: Chrome is open source, and Chromium is Google’s proprietary extension of it.
options.rationale: It is the other way round: Chromium is the open source base.

options.text: Chromium is an email client made by the Chrome team and shares no code with it.
options.rationale: Chromium is a web browser.

options.text: They are two names for the same fully proprietary program.
options.rationale: Chromium is open source and Chrome is not entirely.

options.text: Chromium is the open source browser, and Chrome is built on it with some proprietary parts added.
options.rationale: Chrome adds Google’s own components to the open source base.

explanation: Chromium is the open source browser project. Chrome is Google’s browser built from it with extra proprietary parts.

stem: Mira wants to sign the studio’s release files and encrypt a file for Ada from the terminal. Which tool does that?

options.rationale: VSCodium is a code editor.
GPG (GnuPG) encrypts and signs files and email.
VLC plays audio and video.
R is for statistics and charts.

explanation: GPG is a command line tool for encryption and digital signatures.

stem: Exam 010-160 lists OpenOffice.org next to LibreOffice. What kind of program is it?

options.text: An office suite with a word processor, a spreadsheet and slides.
options.rationale: It is the older suite from which LibreOffice was forked.

options.text: A web browser that is built on top of the Firefox browser engine.
options.rationale: Firefox is the Mozilla browser; OpenOffice.org is office software.

options.text: A package manager for office documents.
options.rationale: It edits documents; it doesn’t install packages.
It is for creating documents, not playing videos.

explanation: OpenOffice.org is the older office suite that LibreOffice was forked from; it lives on as Apache OpenOffice.

stem: Jonas wants to retouch a photo of the team and edit the pixels of a game sprite sheet. Which program is the open source choice for raster images?

options.rationale: Thunderbird is an email client.
GIMP edits photos and other pixel-based images.
Firefox is a web browser.
Writer is a word processor.

explanation: GIMP is the open source raster image editor; Inkscape is its counterpart for vector graphics.

stem: Which open source web browser is developed by the Mozilla community?

options.rationale: Thunderbird is Mozilla’s email client, not its browser.
Calc is a spreadsheet.
Firefox is Mozilla’s browser.
VLC plays media files.

explanation: Firefox is the browser and Thunderbird the mail client, both from Mozilla.

stem: Ada wants to mount a directory from the build server on another Linux machine, as if it were local. Which network file system is built for sharing between Unix and Linux machines?

options.rationale: MariaDB is a database server.
Apache serves web pages.
PostgreSQL is a database server.
The Network File System shares directories between Unix and Linux machines.

explanation: NFS shares directories between Unix and Linux machines; Samba shares files and printers with Windows.

stem: The studio’s apprentices need online courses with quizzes and grades. Which open source platform is made for that?

options.rationale: Kodi is a media center.
Moodle is a learning platform with courses, quizzes and grades.
Jitsi is for video meetings.
Forgejo hosts Git repositories.

explanation: Moodle is a web-based learning management system used by schools and companies.

stem: Ada needs video meetings with the team in a browser, without installing anything. Which open source application does this?

options.rationale: Moodle is a learning platform.
GitLab hosts code and build pipelines.
Jitsi runs video meetings in the browser.
Kodi plays media on a TV.

explanation: Jitsi offers video conferencing in the browser; BigBlueButton is a web conferencing system designed for virtual classrooms.

stem: Jonas wants to turn the studio’s old PC under the TV into a media center for movies, music and photos. Which program fits?

options.rationale: Jitsi is a video conferencing tool.
GIMP edits photos but doesn’t manage a media library.
Nextcloud syncs and shares files, but is not a TV media center.
Kodi is a media center application.

explanation: Kodi is an open source media center for video, music and photos.

stem: Which statement about Git and GitLab is correct?

options.text: Git is a command line tool that tracks changes; GitLab is a web service built around Git repositories.
options.rationale: GitLab adds issue tracking and build pipelines to Git repositories.

options.text: Git is a web application, and GitLab is its command line client.
options.rationale: Git is the command line tool; GitLab is the web application.

options.text: Git and GitLab are two names for the same program.
options.rationale: They are different programs.

options.text: Git is a media center, and GitLab is a video conferencing system.
options.rationale: Neither fits: Git tracks code changes.

explanation: Git tracks changes to source code. GitLab, Forgejo and Gitea are web services that host Git repositories and add features such as issue tracking.

stem: Which two are light, self-hosted Git forges? (Choose TWO.)

options.rationale: Gitea is a similar self-hosted Git forge.
Moodle is for online courses.
Kodi is a media center.
Jitsi is for video meetings.
Forgejo hosts Git repositories and can be run on your own server.

explanation: Forgejo and Gitea are self-hosted Git forges similar in idea to GitLab.

stem: Which of these programs delivers web pages to browsers?

options.rationale: MariaDB is a database server.
Apache HTTPD and NGINX both deliver web pages.
Thunderbird is an email client, a desktop program.
NFS shares directories between Unix and Linux machines.

explanation: Apache HTTPD and NGINX are web servers; NGINX is also often used as a reverse proxy.

stem: Which statement about MariaDB and MySQL is correct?

options.text: Both are database servers, and MariaDB started as a fork of MySQL.
options.rationale: They store structured data and answer queries.

options.text: Both are web servers for static pages, and MySQL started as a fork of MariaDB.
options.rationale: They are database servers, not web servers, and the fork went the other way.

options.text: MariaDB is a programming language and MySQL is its compiler.
options.rationale: Both are database servers.

options.text: Both share files with Windows computers.
options.rationale: Sharing files with Windows is Samba’s job.

explanation: MariaDB, MySQL and PostgreSQL are database servers. LAMP means Linux, Apache, MariaDB or MySQL, and PHP.

stem: The studio’s artists use Windows PCs. Which server program lets Mira share a folder and printers with them from a Linux machine?

options.rationale: NGINX serves web pages.
PostgreSQL stores structured data.
Apache HTTPD serves web pages.
Samba speaks the Windows file and printer sharing protocols.

explanation: Samba shares files and printers with Windows. NFS is the network file system for sharing directories between Unix and Linux machines.

stem: Ada wants a self-hosted file sync and sharing service, similar to Dropbox but on the studio’s own server. Which application fits?

options.rationale: NFS shares directories on a local network; it is not a sync service with a web interface.
PostgreSQL is a database server; it doesn’t sync files between devices.
Nextcloud (and ownCloud) offers file sync, sharing, calendars and contacts.
Moodle is for online courses.

explanation: Nextcloud and ownCloud are server applications for your own file sync and sharing “cloud”.

stem: Which of these are database servers? (Choose TWO.)

options.rationale: MariaDB stores structured data and answers queries.
NFS shares directories over the network.
Samba shares files and printers.
Apache HTTPD is a web server.
PostgreSQL is a database server.

explanation: The database servers in the list are MariaDB, MySQL and PostgreSQL.

stem: Mira reads that the Linux kernel is mostly written in one language. Which?

options.rationale: Python is popular for scripts but not for the kernel.
PHP is used for server-side web pages.
JavaScript is the language of browsers.
Linux is mostly written in C.

explanation: C is used for operating systems, drivers and fast programs, and the kernel is mostly C.

stem: Ada writes short scripts that automate the studio’s builds and analyse data. Which general-purpose language is popular for this?

options.rationale: Python is popular for scripting, automation and data science.
PHP’s main use is server-side web pages.
C++ is typically used for large, speed-critical programs.
Assembly is low-level machine programming, not for quick scripts.

explanation: Python is an interpreted general-purpose language that is popular for scripts and automation.

stem: Jonas wants to add interactivity to the studio’s website that runs inside the visitor’s browser. Which language is for that?

options.rationale: Java runs on the Java virtual machine, in business applications.
JavaScript is the language of web browsers.
C compiles to programs that run outside the browser.
PHP runs on the server, not in the visitor’s browser.

explanation: JavaScript runs in the browser, and also on servers through Node.js. Java is a different language.

stem: Which language is mainly used to produce web pages on a server, for example WordPress or Moodle?

options.rationale: Rust is used for systems programming.
Go is used for network services and tools.
PHP is a server-side language for web pages.
C++ is used for large programs where speed matters, such as games.

explanation: PHP is the “P” in LAMP: it runs on the web server and produces pages.

stem: Which of these languages are compiled to machine code before they run? (Choose THREE.)

options.rationale: JavaScript is run by a browser or Node.js engine.
Python is run by an interpreter.
Rust is compiled.
PHP is run by an interpreter.
C is compiled.
Go is compiled.

explanation: C, C++, Rust and Go are compiled; Python, PHP and JavaScript are interpreted. Java is compiled to bytecode that a virtual machine runs.

stem: Exam 010-160 lists Perl. What is Perl?

options.text: An older scripting language, popular for text processing and system tasks.
options.rationale: Perl is still installed on many Linux systems.

options.text: A compiled language that Linux’s developers use to write the kernel today.
options.rationale: The kernel is mostly C.

options.text: A web browser written in Rust.
options.rationale: Perl is a scripting language.

options.text: A tool for installing packages on Debian.
options.rationale: Packages are installed with `dpkg` and `apt`.

explanation: Perl is an interpreted scripting language that was very popular in the 1990s and 2000s.

stem: Exam 010-160 lists “shell” among the languages. What does that mean?

options.text: A language that only runs inside web browsers.
options.rationale: That describes JavaScript.

options.text: A language that must be compiled with a C compiler first.
options.rationale: Shell scripts are interpreted.

options.text: A language that is used only for designing graphics.
options.rationale: Shell is for commands and scripts.

options.text: Terminal commands can also be written into a script in the shell language.
options.rationale: The shell is a command language that you can also write scripts in.

explanation: Bash, the usual shell, is both the command interpreter and a scripting language.

stem: Ada checks that Perl is installed on the guest and runs a one-line program. What does this command print?
explanation: `perl -e` runs the program given on the command line. `print` writes the text, and `\n` adds a newline.

stem: What is a software repository?

options.text: A folder on the desktop where installed programs store their settings.
options.rationale: A repository is a server, not a local settings folder.

options.text: A server that holds many packages and an index that the package manager downloads.
options.rationale: Distributions run official repositories.

options.text: A program that compiles source code into packages.
options.rationale: Compiling is done by build tools.

options.text: A log file that lists all failed installations.
options.rationale: That is a log, not a repository.

explanation: A package manager downloads the repository index and fetches the packages you ask for, together with what they depend on.

stem: A package declares that it needs other packages to work. What are these called?

options.rationale: Mirrors are copies of a repository on other servers.
A release is a version of the distribution.
The package manager resolves dependencies and installs them with the package.
Maintainer scripts run during installation or removal; they are not the packages it needs.

explanation: A package holds a program, its data files and metadata such as its name, version and dependencies.

stem: Why do distributions sign the packages in their repositories?

options.text: So the system can check a package’s origin and that nobody altered it.
options.rationale: Signatures protect against tampered packages.

options.text: So that only paying customers can install them.
options.rationale: Signing doesn’t restrict who may install.

options.text: So that the packages need fewer dependencies.
options.rationale: Signing has nothing to do with dependencies.

options.text: So that they take less disk space.
options.rationale: Signing doesn’t shrink packages.

explanation: The package manager verifies each package’s signature against the distribution’s key before it installs it.

stem: Mira asks the Debian guest which package supplies the file `/bin/ls`. What does this command print?

options.rationale: The package name comes first, and the package isn’t called `ls`.
The output starts with the package name, then a colon and the path.
`dpkg` is the tool, not a package that contains the file.
`dpkg -S` prints the owning package, a colon and the path.

explanation: `dpkg -S` (`--search`) names the installed package that owns a file: first the package, then a colon and the path.

stem: What is the difference between `dpkg` and `apt`?

options.text: `dpkg` fetches dependencies from repositories, and `apt` handles only single files.
options.rationale: It is the other way round.

options.text: `dpkg` is for Enterprise Linux, and `apt` is for SUSE.
options.rationale: Both belong to the Debian family.

options.text: `dpkg` works on single files and fetches nothing; `apt` uses repositories and resolves dependencies.
options.rationale: `apt` calls `dpkg` underneath.

options.text: They are two names for the same program.
options.rationale: They are separate tools.

explanation: The low-level tool installs or inspects one package file. The high-level tool talks to repositories and resolves dependencies.

stem: Which statement about `apt` and `apt-get` is correct?

options.text: `apt` is meant for RPM packages on Enterprise Linux, and `apt-get` is for Debian packages.
options.rationale: Both work with `.deb` packages.

options.text: `apt` is the friendlier front end for people; `apt-get` is the older one for scripts.
options.rationale: Both manage Debian-family packages.
`apt` is the newer, friendlier one.

options.text: Both can only be used by the root user without `sudo`.
options.rationale: Both can be run with `sudo`, and that isn’t the difference.

explanation: Both belong to the Debian family. Scripts often use `apt-get`, people at the keyboard use `apt`.

stem: Ada logs into a server running openSUSE Leap. Which command installs software from the repositories there?

options.rationale: `dnf` belongs to Enterprise Linux and Fedora.
`zypper` is the SUSE family’s package manager.
`apt` belongs to the Debian family.
`apk` is Alpine Linux’s tool.

explanation: Each family has its own high-level tool: `apt`, `dnf`, `zypper` and `apk`.

stem: Which Alpine Linux command-line tool installs and removes packages? Type its name.
explanation: `apk` (Alpine Package Keeper) is Alpine’s package manager, for example `apk add gimp` as root.

stem: Mira wants to list all packages installed on the Debian guest. Type the `dpkg` command with its short option.
explanation: `dpkg -l` (`--list`) lists installed packages; `dpkg -L` would list the files of one package instead.

stem: Mira wants to know which installed package supplies the file `/bin/ls`. Complete the `dpkg` command with the search option and the path.
explanation: `dpkg -S` (`--search`) searches for the package that owns a file.

stem: Jonas asks the Debian guest which of the tools `dpkg` and `rpm` are installed. What does this command print?
command: for t in dpkg rpm; do command -v $t || echo "no $t"; done
explanation: `command -v` prints the path of a program that exists. The guest is Debian, so it has `dpkg` and not `rpm`.

stem: Exam 010-160 lists `yum` instead of `dnf`. What was `yum`?

options.text: The Red Hat family’s package tool, which `dnf` replaced.
options.rationale: `yum install gimp` did what `dnf install gimp` does today.

options.text: The low-level tool that Debian uses for installing single `.deb` files.
options.rationale: Debian’s low-level tool is `dpkg`.

options.text: The package manager of Alpine Linux.
options.rationale: Alpine uses `apk`.

options.text: A SUSE tool for installing RPM files.
options.rationale: SUSE uses `zypper`.

explanation: yum shipped with older versions of RHEL and CentOS and used the same `.rpm` packages.
